title: FACT CHECK: PhilHealth not offering P5,000 cash aid under YAKAP
summary: PhilHealth has no program that automatically provides cash assistance to all its members

blocks.text: Claim: The Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) will provide P5,000 cash aid to all its members through its Yaman ng Kalusugan Program (YAKAP).

Why we fact-checked this: Facebook user Cres Jhoerax Vlog posted a video bearing the claim on November 20. The video claims that all PhilHealth members — regardless of whether they are active or inactive paying members — are eligible for the supposed P5,000 cash payout.
It also claims that even those without a Member Data Record or ID are eligible for the cash assistance.

“Nasa aming post ang registration, ang mga requirement, at iba pang detalye. Paki-share po sa iba, para mas marami ang makaalam at makapag-register nang maaga. Mag-follow sa amin at i-share ang balitang ito,” a narrator says in the video.

(Our post contains information regarding registration, requirements, and other details. Please share it with others so that more people can be informed and register early. Follow us and share this news.)
The video has garnered over 100 comments and 200 shares as of writing. Other users have reposted the video bearing the same claim.
The facts: PhilHealth has debunked circulating posts claiming that YAKAP provides cash aid to members.
The agency clarified that it has no program offering cash assistance to all its members, as its mandate is to provide health insurance coverage and access to healthcare services.

The health insurer urged the public to be wary of posts promising unconditional cash assistance or announcing supposed payout schedules accompanied by dubious registration links, particularly those that did not come from any of PhilHealth’s official accounts.
YAKAP is PhilHealth’s national primary care benefit package, giving its members free access to primary care services at accredited clinics. It is an improved version of its Konsulta program.
The program’s benefits include free checkups, laboratory tests, medicines, and cancer screening tests.

AI-generated video, dubious info: The videos about the supposed cash aid are AI-generated. Detection tool HumanMeter flagged one of the videos as 95% likely to be AI-generated, while HiveModeration gave an AI likelihood score of 94.7%.

Meanwhile, similar videos about PhilHealth’s supposed P5,000 cash aid mistakenly reference “AKAP” — referring to the Ayuda para sa Kapos ang Kita Program of the Department of Social Welfare and Development.

Though this program provided cash assistance, it was intended for individuals whose income is insufficient to meet their basic needs. The program has been discontinued as of 2026 and is not affiliated with PhilHealth.
